subject: Discovery recap: Private / VPC / KMS / air-gap requirements — MediTrace Health
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chu <michael.chu@meditrace.health>, Dr. Sara Khan <sara.khan@meditrace.health>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Private / VPC / KMS / air-gap requirements — MediTrace Health

Hi Michael / Sara — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has a shared view and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Strict regulatory requirement for PHI data to never egress to public internet and to be restricted to an approved VPC/on-prem setup.
- Need for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) with FIPS-140-2 compatibility and key rotation control.
- Very limited outbound connectivity from inference hosts (no internet egress allowed for runtime).
- High availability SLO for inference on core triage flows (sub-second p50 target, predictable throughput for overnight batch processing).

Current environment (what you told us):
- Production is on-prem Kubernetes (RHEL nodes) behind strict firewall/appliance (Palo Alto).
- Authentication: SAML + internal IdP; they use an internal KMS tied to HSM for key material.
- Network: isolated VLANs, NAT egress tightly controlled; procurement requires explicit IP allowlist and egress rules.

Success criteria for a PoC / pilot:
1) Deployment in MediTrace VPC or private subnet with no outbound internet from inference nodes.
2) Demonstrate inference with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS or HSM integration).
3) Latency validation on the triage flow: p50 < 500ms, p95 < 2s at 50 RPS.
4) Security review: provide network-capture checklist, SOC2 evidence, and notes on audit logging.

Open questions / clarifications needed from your side:
- Can you share a sanitized network diagram and firewall policy for the inference subnet? (we included a template attached).
- Does the internal KMS expose an API we can integrate with, or would you prefer an HSM appliance connector?
- Are there designated IP ranges we should plan to request for allowlisting for initial PoC?

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Vivek (SE) to run a technical deep-dive focused on KMS/HSM integration and offline deployment constraints — target week of Aug 31.
- MediTrace to share network diagram + example KMS policy by Aug 28 — OWNER: Michael.
- Camila to send a short Mutual Action Plan (timeline + success criteria) and an initial estimate for Dedicated + Private pricing — by Aug 26.
- Monica (CS) to start documenting support and SLA expectations for an air-gapped deployment.

Attachments: redwood-private-capabilities.pdf, network-firewall-template.xlsx (attachment stubs included).

If that matches your view, I’ll draft a short MAP and propose a PoC kickoff window (we suggested Sep 7–10).

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime and private deployment options.
From: Michael Chu <michael.chu@meditrace.health>

Cc: Dr. Sara Khan <sara.khan@meditrace.health>, procurement@meditrace.health
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private / VPC / KMS / air-gap requirements — MediTrace Health

Camila — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Environment detail: Production runs in our on-prem K8s cluster (RHEL 8) with strict egress rules. Staging can be opened up more for PoC but production nodes cannot have outbound internet.
- KMS: we run a Thales Luna HSM cluster; we can expose a signed API endpoint for the PoC but anything in prod must call the HSM through our internal network only.
- Network constraints: no external package pulls allowed from inference nodes; images must be delivered via our internal registry.
- Compliance: we need documentation for audit logging (who accessed keys, model inference logs) for a SOC2+HIPAA review.

Procurement notes: procurement@meditrace.health copied — our procurement window is FY-end Sep 30. For PoC budgeting: please include both (a) Dedicated GPU pool in Redwood hosted in our cloud VPC, and (b) Private installer pricing (one-time + annual support).

I attached a short doc that highlights differences between what we run in staging vs prod (mt-network-diff.pdf).

Michael
Michael Chu
IT Infrastructure Manager | MediTrace Health
michael.chu@meditrace.health

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private / VPC / KMS / air-gap requirements — MediTrace Health

Appreciate the details, Michael — this is exactly helpful. Two quick confirmations and what we’ll do next:

Confirmations:
- We can support images via a customer-internal registry and will not require runtime egress for package pulls if images and dependencies are pre-seeded.
- We have connectors for Thales Luna (SE team will validate firmware/driver compatibility during the deep-dive).

Immediate next steps (concrete):
1) Vivek — can you prepare a 60–90 minute SE session that covers: HSM connector options, installer packaging to run entirely in our air-gapped mode, and what logs/audit artifacts Redwood can produce? Proposed slot: Sep 2 or Sep 3.
2) Michael — if you can upload the sanitized network diagram + KMS access pattern to the Drive folder I linked, that will accelerate scoping.
3) Camila (me) — I’ll send the Mutual Action Plan PDF and initial commercial sketch (Dedicated + Private) by EOD Aug 26.
4) Monica — please start drafting language around data handling + air-gap support in our standard SOW template; we may need addenda for HSM and offline upgrades.

Attachments: I’m including the private capabilities PDF and a short checklist for air-gapped installs.

Thanks — aiming to lock the PoC kickoff week (Sep 7) pending your diagram and Vivek availability.

Best,
Camila
